findings.title: Cleanup registers the literal alias "alias" instead of the created provider alias
findings.body: In the new testCacheIDPForLogin, cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` using the string literal "alias" rather than the alias of the provider just created (`"idp-alias-" + i`; the same mistake is repeated on line 425 for `idp-alias-20`). At teardown this invokes remove() on a non-existent provider (typically a 404/WebApplicationException, which can fail the test teardown), and none of the 20+ `idp-alias-*` providers the test creates are ever deleted. They leak into the realm and can break later tests in the class that assume a clean IDP set or re-create the same aliases. It should use `idpRep.getAlias()` (or `"idp-alias-" + i`) in the cleanup.

findings.title: Login-cache invalidation on update computes the 'original' state from an org-aware wrapper, so disabling an IDP of a disabled org is not invalidated
findings.body: In update(), `original` is obtained via `getById(model.getInternalId())`, which returns `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(...)` whose `isEnabled()` returns false when the linked organization is disabled (see line 141 and 436-443). However the login cache is populated from the raw `enabled` column (the delegate's `getForLogin`/`getAllStream` ignores organization enabled state), so an IDP linked to a currently-disabled organization is present in the cached login list while `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` evaluates to false for it. `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` then hits the `!predicate(original) && !predicate(updated)` early-return at line 405 and skips invalidation when that IDP's own `enabled` flag is set to false, leaving a now-disabled IDP in the cached list returned by `getForLogin` (violating the method contract that it returns login-eligible IDPs). create()/remove() use raw (un-wrapped) models, so update() is inconsistent with them. The original state used for the login predicate should be the raw model (e.g. from `idpDelegate`), not the organization-aware wrapper.

findings.title: New remove() login invalidation path is only tested with a non-login IDP
findings.body: The test removes `idp-alias-1`, which was created disabled (`enabled = (i % 2) == 0`), so it only exercises the negative branch of the newly added remove() logic (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)` where the provider is not login-eligible and therefore must not invalidate the caches). No test removes an enabled, public IDP and asserts that the login caches ARE cleared, so the positive invalidation path added to remove() is untested; a regression there (or an NPE/pruning of the newly introduced `storedIdp` lookup) would go unnoticed.
